findings.evidence: Lines 381-383 are the only use of `hrolle`/`hp` (`thomEncoding_injOn p hrolle hp ha hb heq`). `hpos` (393-397) uses `ha`/`hb`, but `hs` (387-389) already witnesses `i.val + 1 ∈ s`, so `Finset.le_max' s (i.val+1)` yields `1 ≤ k` unconditionally. `hdeg` (398-400) and the tail (402-410) invoke only `derivativeSign_const` (142), which is in the `[Semiring R] [LinearOrder R]` section ending at line 158; `Finset.filter` is fine since `SignType` has `DecidableEq`.
findings.fix: State the extraction in the `Basic` section as `theorem exists_derivativeSign_ne (p : R[X]) {a b : R} (h : thomEncoding p a ≠ thomEncoding p b) : ∃ k, 0 < k ∧ k < p.natDegree ∧ derivativeSign p a k ≠ derivativeSign p b k ∧ ∀ j, k < j → derivativeSign p a j = derivativeSign p b j`, with the same `Finset.max'` proof; then derive the root-pair versions (roots + `hrolle` + `hp`) from it via `thomEncoding_injOn`, and likewise rebase `exists_thomEncoding_ne`.
findings.issue: `exists_derivativeSign_ne` (376) and its finite version `exists_thomEncoding_ne` (413) assume `hrolle`, `hp`, `ha : p.eval a = 0`, `hb : p.eval b = 0`, but the content is the combinatorial extraction of a maximal differing index, valid at `[Semiring R] [LinearOrder R]` from `thomEncoding p a ≠ thomEncoding p b` alone. This blocks the PR's own arbitrary-point comparison lemmas `lt_iff_derivativeSign` (302) and `lt_iff_thomEncoding` (337), whose `hne`/`htail` premises nothing in the PR can supply for a point that is not a root.

summary: Assumptions are minimal and used throughout except in the maximal-differing-index extraction, where Rolle, `p ≠ 0`, and both root hypotheses are all discharged by the single weaker hypothesis `thomEncoding p a ≠ thomEncoding p b`, leaving a purely combinatorial statement stranded in the Field+Rolle section. Everything else sits at the natural level, with each `Fin p.natDegree` result derived from its ℕ-indexed general form.
